ruling.recommended_action: Determine the correct flagdown/distance/time fare for the quoted 10.761 km / 17.3 min route under the taxi company's meter and refund the excess collected plus any tolls charged; do not, on this record, treat the trip as a valid metered fare — the meter and time figures in the record are mutually inconsistent. Re-request the full GPS trace and the meter data before finalising the amount. Record the driver's RD-1 breach (unsolicited deviation around the Ayer Rajah Expressway).

segment_findings.reason: The quoted route (10.761 km) proceeds to NUS largely along the Ayer Rajah Expressway / Central Expressway corridor, while the thin GPS trace shows the driver turning off around 22:53–22:57 into the East Coast / Marine Parade area at ~8 km/h before turning back NW — consistent with the deviation the rider complains about and admitted in the driver's statement ('I went round it'). Its extent cannot be measured because the trace is thinned to every 6th sample (~370 m between measured points) and the record's figures conflict (fare 12.41 km vs rider's 12 km vs ~12.1 km traceable), so RD-1/RD-2 cannot be quantified. RD-4 does not exempt it: incidents = [] (no LTA incident on the replaced optimum-route segment), and RD-4(b) forbids sole reliance on the Ayer Rajah Expressway / Central Expressway band-1 records (they are only corroborative). No rider consent (RD-5) appears in the chat, and RD-3 is not invoked by any rider stop/destination change. Undetermined → escalate for a human to fix the amount.

rejected_claims.reason: The claim that Ayer Rajah Expressway was 'crawling' is not supported by any LTA incident on the replaced optimum-route segment (incidents = []); the band-1 speed records on Ayer Rajah Expressway (SYN-1002) and Central Expressway (SYN-0007) are, under RD-4(b), only corroborative and cannot justify a sola exemption.

RD-5 consent cannot be found: the chat contains only pickup-arrangement messages (blue shirt / white Honda Vezel) and no message from the rider agreeing to any route change before the deviation began. The driver's statement contains no consent claim either.

Not accepted as a metre reading: distance_fare = 17.50 contradicts the stated per-km rate (12.41 × 1.41 = 17.50 implies the $20.40 base is 12.41 × 1.64), and the flat quote arithmetic fits the quoted 10.761 km. The fare block therefore cannot be reconciled with the quoted route's meter fare and cannot be used as the basis of the RD-2 calculation without the full meter data.
